title: Cap. VIII critique: Corvinus's vocabulary of unbelief and vocation against Scripture; original sin alone
pass_a_gloss: Further, when in constituting their sentence they say that God in the decree of reprobation considers men as actually unbelieving and impenitent against God actually calling, they are compelled to use vocabularies against the received custom of the sacred Scriptures and of almost all Theologians. For if we will take the norm of speaking from the Scriptures and from sound Theologians, unbelief denotes rejection of the Gospel, and the vocabularies of grace and of vocation presuppose the manifestation of the Gospel. But by Arminius and Corvinus they are reprobated on account of foresighted unbelief, to whom the Gospel was never announced; they are said to have rejected grace and vocation, to whom the grace of Christ was never offered. Finally, what they teach concerning original sin, that it by no means makes any man guilty of eternal death, nor that anyone is damned on account of that alone, this truly is as alien from the doctrine of the catholic Church as it is necessarily conjoined and connected with Arminian Theology.
pass_b_english: Further: when they say that in the reprobation decree God considers men as actually unbelieving and impenitent against God actually calling, they are forced to use words against the received custom of Scripture and of almost all theologians. If we take our speaking-norm from Scripture and sound theologians, unbelief denotes rejection of the Gospel, and the words grace and vocation presuppose the Gospel's manifestation. Yet on Arminius's and Corvinus's view, people are reprobated for foresighted unbelief to whom the Gospel was never announced, and said to have rejected grace and vocation to whom Christ's grace was never offered. Finally, their teaching that original sin makes no man guilty of eternal death, and that no one is damned for that alone, is as alien to the catholic Church's doctrine as it is necessarily bound up with Arminian theology.
source_text: Porro, quando in constituenda sua sententia dicunt, Deum in decreto reprobationis considerare homines ut actu infideles et impenitentes contra Deum actu vocantem, coguntur vocabulis uti contra receptam sacrarum Scripturarum et omnium fere Theologorum consuetudinem. Si enim norman loquendi a Scripturis et sanis Theologis accipere velimus, infidelitas denotat rejectionem Evangelii, et vocabula gratiae ac vocationis Evangelii patefactionem praesupponunt. At Arminio et Corvino ob infidelitatem praevisam reprobantur, quibus Evangelium nunquam fuit annuntiatum; gratiam ac vocationem rejecisse dicuntur, quibus gratia Christi nunquam fuit oblata. Denique, quod de originali peccato docent, illud haud facere ullum hominem aeternae mortis reum, nec propter illud solum quenquam damnari, hoc profecto tam alienum est a catholicae Ecclesiae doctrina, quam est cum Arminiana Theologia necessario conjunctum et connexum.
